verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 8.2 item 7: 'Links: the sandbox with this module's board loaded; the Atlas page; the next module.' The sentence has no label, and SPEC does not define 'this module's board'. SPEC 3 M7 table row 1 says 'T10, root polytope of A2, then A3, then D4'. 8.1 P3 says 'Each module starts on A2 or A3'. decisions/P4-A6.md, 'the module's board for the sandbox link', is a builder's choice taken from the plan. It is not a [D] text, a D1-D19 default or an owner's answer.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 with git show; nothing built or run. m7-geometry.mdx:189 is '<ModuleLinks module={7} board="B3" />'. M7 b1 is T10 root-polytope on A2 (line 58). The other lessons pass A3, A2, A3, A3, A2, A3 and B2 for M0 to M6; M1, M3 and M4 match their first figures since round 1. Records: (1) decisions/P4-A6.md says 'Decision: <ModuleLinks module={7} board="B3" />: B3 carries the face table, make uniform and two challenges.' The plan instruction behind it is build-plan/agents/P4-A6-lesson-m7.md:214: 'SPEC 3 does not name M7's board; choose one the module touches (B3 or E8) and record it (plan)'. No 'Deviations accepted' entry for P4-A6 in DECISIONS.md (MERGE P4 entries at lines 2501 and 2642) mentions it, and no OWNER entry does. (2) The round 1 fragments RT-FIX-P3-lesson-m1.md, -m3.md and -m4.md each adopt 'the board of the first figure' for their own module. They cite RT-13 attack 17 and 'confirmed by both verifiers of P3-RT-13-05', and -m3 says the earlier choice from a plan instruction was 'not a [D] text of the specification, a default of section 10 or an owner's answer'. P4-A6's choice is the same kind of record. (3) The round 1 refute verdict on P3-RT-13-05 (round1-confirmed-B.json) failed R5 for the same reason: the choices were recorded only as agent choices (plan). (4) The 'known and decided' list and the MERGE round 1 entry hold only the order of the module links of 8.2 item 7, not the board. (5) reports/gate-G4.md (report commit, naming gate commit b9b8504) says nothing about the sandbox board. No merge-P4-redteam report exists on disk.
verdicts.reason: not refuted. R1 fails: 8.2 item 7 has no qualifier, and no SPEC sentence names B3 as M7's board; the [D] of the SPEC 3 preamble covers the figure configurations, not the link. R2 fails: the finding quotes 8.2 item 7 correctly and presents the first-figure reading as the reading of the round 1 records, not as SPEC text; 8.1 P3 leans its way. R3 fails: M7 and T16 are phases 4 and 2, both within G4. R4 does not apply: no oracle value is involved. R5 fails: decisions/P4-A6.md is a logged builder choice made on a plan instruction, not a [D] text, a section 10 default or an owner's answer, and the round 1 fixers replaced records of exactly this kind. R6 fails: no gate or merge record holds the M7 board. For the owner: 'this module's board' is undefined for a module with several boards, and the plan's instruction (B3 or E8) contradicts the lens's reading (A2). A wrong stated behaviour is major, as claimed.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 8.3 Visual language [D]: the accents 'mark the borders and icons of panels and the underlines of the two words' and the icons are 'used wherever the view is named'. 6.3 [D]: 'The Populations view and the Numbers view have distinct, fixed accent colours and icons used consistently in prose, figures and formulas (principle P8)'. 8.1 P8. All three support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 with git show. m7-geometry.mdx:65 ends with 'Rings are numbers, so this module uses the Numbers view.' as plain text. The counts of data-view-word, View and ViewWord per lesson are m0 4, m4 3 and 0 in m1, m2, m3, m5, m6 and m7. M5 and M6 have no prose naming of a view, so M7 is the only unmarked naming. The view words are in fact marked by local helpers: View is defined in m0-start.mdx:21 and ViewWord in m4-numbers.mdx:24. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-lesson-m0.md, 'request, one shared component for the view words', asks MERGE to share the helper 'so that M4 and later lessons use one implementation'. No MERGE, OWNER or GATE entry accepts unmarked view words in later lessons. The MERGE entry of 2026-10-24 lists P3-RT-13-08 as 'Confirmed fixed', not held. decisions/P4-A6.md has no entry on view words. 8.3 has no 'may' or 'where ... allows'. gate-G4.md says nothing about accents.
verdicts.reason: not refuted. R1 fails: 8.3 and 6.3 say 'wherever the view is named' and 'in prose' with no permitting clause. R2 fails: the finding quotes 8.3 and P8 correctly, and line 65 names the Numbers view. R3 fails: M7 is phase 4, within G4, and 8.3 carries no phase. R4 does not apply. R5 fails: 8.3 is [D], but the build departs from its text, and no record accepts the departure; the M0 fixer's request for a shared component was never acted on or waived. R6 fails: P3-RT-13-08 is recorded as fixed, so this is a sibling recurrence in a new lesson, not a held duplicate. A stated behaviour that is missing is major, as claimed.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 1.3 LO6: 'read a multiple edge with an arrow as long and short roots'. 1.2: the primary reader should leave with 'the ability to read a Dynkin or Satake diagram'. 2.1 (unlabelled, so a definition under 0.3): '(2,1) and (3,1) are a double and a triple line with an arrowhead pointing from i to j, the direction in which the extra roads run'. SPEC 3 M6 assigns LO6. 6.2 [D] covers only which drawing style is used, not whether it is explained.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 with git show. m0-start.mdx:37: 'A line between two nodes stands for one road running each way.' This is the only drawing rule in M0 to M6; a grep for line, lines, arrowhead, chevron and 'drawn as' finds no other. M6 sets roadStyle="roads" only on b1 (line 82) and b12 (line 206). b3 (B2), b4 (G2) and b11 (G2) pass no roadStyle, so they take 6.2's default `dynkin` style: 'one, two or three parallel lines ... a chevron'. DECISIONS.md:520 records that roadGlyphs draws `lines` with a chevron. Roads.svelte is aria-hidden, and the tool shows no legend. The only arrow sentence is in the LieTheory paragraph (m6:194): 'The arrow of a Dynkin diagram points from the long simple root to the short one.' Beat 3 says 'more roads run from the long city to the short one' but never ties this to the double line or the chevron. The glossary has no entry for the drawing (only black, white and arrows for Satake). 6.2 [D] allows `dynkin` as the default and names M6 for `roads` 'where the counts in each direction are the subject'. That permits the drawing, not the missing reading rule. decisions/P4-A5.md records the roads style of b1 and nothing on explaining the dynkin drawing. No MERGE, OWNER or gate-G4 record touches it. The finding's matrix [[2,-2],[-2,2]] for two roads each way is correct under 2.1 (C = 2I - A^T).
verdicts.reason: not refuted. R1 fails: no sentence permits leaving the double or triple line and the chevron unexplained to the primary reader, and 6.2 [D] governs the choice of style, not its explanation. R2 fails: LO6, 1.2 and 2.1 say what the finding says, and the only rule M0 gives contradicts the drawing on b3, b4 and b11. R3 fails: M6 is phase 4 and SPEC 3 gives it LO6. R4 does not apply: the claim is about teaching, not a value. R5 fails: the build follows the [D] of 6.2, but the defect is the missing reading rule, which no [D] text, section 10 default or record covers. R6 fails: there is no record. A stated behaviour that is missing, or a prose rule of 8.4 broken (define on first use), is major, as claimed.

verdicts.citation: R2, with support from R1. The SPEC binds a tool's caption to its default (starting) state. SPEC 4.0 [D] 'Works before and without JavaScript': 'The default state of every tool is rendered to HTML and SVG at build time, with its caption.' 7.4 'Without JavaScript': 'Each tool therefore ships its default state as real markup: the SVG board with its values, the caption ...'. 9.2: '(default state with a caption, ...)'. 8.1 P1: 'Each tool has a meaningful starting state and a caption that states its point.' SPEC 6.6: 'A key that is absent keeps the value the page author configured for that instance (on a tool's own route: the tool's default), so a link changes only what it names'. The caption is not a field of the 6.6 state table. Where SPEC wants a caption to follow the play, it says so for that tool: T9 'From phase 2 the caption names that board'; 3 M1 row 2 'the caption says so after 20 moves'. It says nothing like this for T10 or T16. decisions/P1-A2.md (tools route): 'The tool receives id="" (bare keys), caption (the default preset's) and preset="default".'
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 with git show. site/src/pages/tools/[tool].astro:46: const toolProps = { id: '', caption, preset: 'default' }, with caption taken from toolRoutes (the registry's presets.default.caption, decisions/P1-A2.md). DECISIONS.md:1271 (P2-A5) records T16's default board (the three-roads-each-way board of bigint_test) and its caption. That caption is true of the default state, which is what 4.0, 7.4, 9.2 and P1 attach it to. 6.6 lists the state fields (schema, tool, board, view, mode, coords, start, moves and tool-specific keys); the caption is a configured property (CONTRACTS 5.2 'presets: { default: { caption } }'; CONTRACTS 7 'Every tool has a caption prop stating the result it demonstrates'), which no link key can change. 8.2 item 7 asks only that the module's board be loaded, and the finding's own observed shows it loaded (B2, verdict 'finite B2'). SPEC 3 M7 row 7 asks for 'static table of the four shells with T10 links', which the observed also shows (E8, 2160 vertices). T11's caption that follows the state is P4-A4's own choice (DECISIONS.md:2211, 'P4-A4: the caption follows the state'), not a SPEC rule. No SPEC sentence requires a caption generated for a state loaded from a link. 'Starts meaningful' speaks of the state a tool loads in and of the surrounding prose, and for the M7 shell links that prose (beat 7) states the shell sizes. 4.0 is a [D] heading, and the build stays within its text.
verdicts.reason: The finding applies P1 and 4.0's caption rule to states loaded by a link, but those passages, with 7.4 and 9.2, attach the caption to the tool's default (starting) state. 6.6 makes a link change only the state keys it names, and the caption is not one of them. SPEC asks for a state-dependent caption only for named cases (T9, M1 row 2), none of them T10 or T16. 8.2 item 7 and M7 row 7 are met, since the links load the board and the orbit. A caption that follows every state would be a new requirement for the owner to decide, as T11's own recorded choice shows.
